summary: For a Ranger on Home level 4, JavaScript computes the role-specific Ran-filb quest filler name but has no loader entry, so generation falls through to the ordinary maze path instead of loading dat/Ran-filb.lua. The complete Lua program and its production loader entry are the bounded source task.

source.branch: When mklev.c:makelevel() creates a Ranger quest filler at or below the locate level, it forms Ran-filb and mkmaze.c:makemaz() loads the whole special-level program. Ran-filb.lua runs solidfill, mazelevel/noflip, a smoothed joined/walled Mines background with blank foreground, up/down stairs, eleven random objects, four random traps, four hostile mountain centaurs, a hostile random C-class monster, and two hostile scorpions, in that order.
callers: mklev.c:makelevel() -> mkmaze.c:makemaz() -> sp_lev.c:load_special() -> dat/Ran-filb.lua top-level statements.
js/mklev.js:760-772 computes the role-specific filler name and calls makemaz() only when SPECIAL_LEVEL_LOADERS contains Ran-filb.
dependencies: The registered special-level path already runs dat/nhlib.lua alignment initialization before the program body.
All level descriptors in Ran-filb.lua use the existing des API.

evidence: Source: nethack-c/upstream/src/mklev.c:1283-1285 selects the later quest filler at or below the locate level; mkmaze.c:makemaz() delegates to sp_lev.c:load_special(); nethack-c/upstream/dat/Ran-filb.lua:6-39 contains the complete program.

Dispatch trace: js/mklev.js:764-772 computes the role-specific fill name, but js/quest_levels.js:QUEST_LEVEL_LOADERS has no Ran-filb entry; therefore the source program does not run and ordinary maze generation continues.
